descriptionChirho: The basic Qal meaning of goring with horns, describing an ox or bull attacking by thrusting its horns. English 'gores' / 'it-gores', Spanish 'acornea' (to gore), Arabic 'nataha' (to butt), Korean 'bad-eumyeon' (if it gores), Swahili 'atampiga pembe' (strikes with horn), Hindi 'maare sing' (strikes with horn). This is the literal, physical action of an animal goring, as in the laws of Exodus 21 regarding an ox that gores.

The Piel intensive stem denoting vigorous or repeated goring and pushing, used both literally of animals and figuratively of military conquest (Deut 33:17). English 'you will gore' / 'butting' / 'we push down' / 'he gores' / 'you-gore', Spanish 'cornearas' / 'acorneando' / 'acornearemos', Arabic 'tantahu' / 'yantahu', Korean 'bad-eurira' (will gore), Swahili 'utawasukuma' (you will push them), Hindi 'sing marta tha' (was goring). The Piel intensifies the action beyond simple goring to aggressive thrusting and pushing down of enemies.

labelChirho: engage in battle, butt against (Hitpael reflexive)
descriptionChirho: The Hitpael reflexive/reciprocal stem meaning to engage mutually in battle or charge against one another, found in Daniel 11:40. English 'shall engage in battle', Spanish 'se embestira' (will charge), Arabic 'yatanatahu' (reciprocal butting), Korean 'bad-eurira', Swahili 'atapigana naye' (will fight with him), Hindi 'sing marega'. The Hitpael transforms the physical goring metaphor into reciprocal military confrontation between opposing kings.
